title: Romanticism
summary: Romanticism was a European movement in all the arts, at its height in Britain from about 1785 to 1825; the term itself came from Germany. Its founding voice was Rousseau, who taught that passion speaks truer than reason, and it put imagination, emotion, nature and the inner self at the centre of art. In Jena around 1798 Friedrich and August Schlegel, Novalis and Schleiermacher published the Athenaeum fragments, while in England Wordsworth and Coleridge issued Lyrical Ballads that year. A second generation, Keats and Shelley among them, followed.

uncertainty.note: The Oxford Companion dates its height in Britain to 1785-1825; the German Jena circle flourished c. 1796-1801.
